newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy hard left still unhappy about welfare reform.
newsitem.headline: Italy hard left still unhappy about welfare reform.

text.p: A leader of Italy's hard left Communist Refoundation party said on Thursday he still had objections to rolling back welfare provisions after a meeting with Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

Oliviero Diliberto, leader of the Refoundation's parliamentary party, said after the meeting that the government, which is preparing a three-year economic strategy, appeared to have shown more flexibility but had not given enough ground.
"We maintain our reservations because it does not appear to me that there has been significant enough progress to make us modify our position," Diliberto told reports after the meeting.
The cabinet is due to approve the plan, which sets taxing and spending plans for the next three years, on Friday.

Communist Refoundation, which the government relies on to secure its majority in the lower house of parliament, is opposed to government proposals to make it harder for people to retire early. The party also opposes any tax on pensions.
"These concerns are not only ours, they have also been expressed by trade unions, therefore we are in good company," he added.
Prodi met allied parliamentary party leaders, including Diliberto, for about one hour on Thursday morning.
Prodi later met trade union leaders ahead of a three-party meeting at 1500 gmt between the government, trade unions and employers. Rome bureau +396-6782560
